title: Eviction orchestration for GPU fragmentation and cache linearizability
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement an eviction orchestration layer that coordinates LRU/TTL/prefix-aware eviction across the continuous batcher and the GPU slab allocator to reduce fragmentation, maintain KV-cache linearizability guarantees for in-flight requests, and reclaim memory predictably without introducing correctness regressions.
background: We observe two correlated problems under high concurrency: (1) GPU slab fragmentation due to many small prefix-scoped KV allocations causing inability to fit new model state despite overall free memory, and (2) correctness/consistency anomalies when eviction and continuous batching overlap (requests reading prefix keys while eviction is reclaiming them). Current heuristics (best-effort LRU + periodic TTL sweep) reduce pressure but do not provide strong safety invariants or predictable latency under bursty workloads.
goals: 1) Provide an eviction protocol that is safe for in-flight batched requests (no stale or missing KV reads). 2) Reduce GPU fragmentation and improve allocator compaction friendliness. 3) Offer measurable SLO-friendly eviction latency and memory reclaim timelines. 4) Allow canary rollout with feature flag and detailed observability.
proposed_solution: Introduce a lease-based eviction orchestrator with epoched compaction windows and prefix coalescing: a) Each KV allocation carries a lightweight lease epoch. b) Eviction candidates are selected by hybrid score (LRU recency + TTL age + prefix-affinity penalty). c) Before reclaim, the orchestrator performs a two-phase withdrawal: mark-for-evict (fast, non-destructive pointer state) then compact after ensuring no active leases reference affected slabs. d) Continuous batcher consults the orchestrator for read semantics: reads pin the prefix epoch; writes/update extend or bump the lease. e) Compaction operates on slab-aligned groups to reduce fragmentation and is scheduled when free contiguous slab run falls below threshold.
correctness_guarantees: We target linearizability for KV read/write semantics as observed by a single request: any read that begins before an eviction commit must either see the pre-eviction value or a clearly defined post-eviction value according to the orchestrator's epoch ordering. Eviction must not cause silent data loss for any in-flight batched request. We provide a formal invariant sketch and an implementation checklist to enforce this at runtime.
invariants: 1) Monotonic epoch assignments per prefix; 2) Lease pin prevents reclamation until all readers with earlier epochs complete; 3) Mark-for-evict is idempotent and reversible until compaction commit; 4) Compaction commits mutate slab ownership atomically with a commit epoch; 5) Batch processing must register epoch pins at dequeue time.
protocol_sketch: 1) Allocation: attach prefix and assign current prefix-epoch. 2) Read path: batch dequeue adds epoch pin to batch context; reads consult cache and may hit marked-for-evict entries but treat them as valid until compaction commit. 3) Eviction selection: compute hybrid score across candidates; prefer slab-coalescing sets. 4) Mark phase: set mark-for-evict and emit event to tracer. 5) Drain phase: wait for epoch pins older than mark to clear (bounded wait with priority fallback). 6) Commit compaction: atomically update slab ownership and free contiguous runs. 7) Fallback: if bounded wait exceeds threshold and memory pressure is critical, fall back to conservative per-key migration into reserved cache area then compact.
implementation_tasks: Extend allocator to expose slab run metadata and compaction API
Implement epoch/lease metadata on KV entries and batch contexts
Add hybrid scoring function (LRU + TTL + prefix-affinity) with tunable weights
Build mark-for-evict / commit state machine and idempotent APIs
Integrate orchestrator hooks into continuous batcher read path
Implement compaction worker that operates on slab-aligned groups
Feature flag gating and runtime knobs (wait thresholds, score weights, slab thresholds)
Instrumentation: traces, events, and histograms for eviction latency and reclaimed runs
testing_strategy: Unit tests for lease lifecycle and mark/commit idempotency
Deterministic integration tests that simulate batched reads/writes + eviction under stress
Fuzz harness that injects delayed batch completions and forced compaction to find races
Property-based tests asserting linearizability for single-key and prefix-scoped operations
Benchmarks comparing fragmentation (largest free run) and tail latency with/without orchestrator
rollout_plan: Start behind feature flag in canary region with synthetic traffic (phase 1). If basic metrics stable, open to internal beta (phase 2) exercised by select customers on Dedicated. Phase 3: global rollout with incremental weight and automated rollback on violation of safety or SLO thresholds.
tradeoffs: - Stronger safety (longer waits for pins) increases OOM risk under extreme pressure. - Aggressive compaction reduces fragmentation but may increase short-term CPU utilization and jitter. - Hybrid scoring can mis-prioritize low-value prefixes; needs empirical tuning per workload.
open_questions: What is an acceptable bounded wait deadline for pinned epochs before triggering fallback?
Should we prefer per-prefix tombstones or live migration into a reserved slab area for immediate reclamation?
How should weights for LRU/TTL/prefix-affinity be exposed to customers vs kept internal?
